name: Pethahiah
overview: Pethahiah was a male member of the tribe of Judah who served as the king's representative in all matters concerning the people. His role, as recorded in Nehemiah 11:24, highlights his official capacity in the governance and oversight of the community during the post-exilic period. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Pethahiah means 'YHWH opens,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the Lord's action or provision. This proper name is noted in Nehemiah 11:24 and does not indicate that it was given directly by God, but it carries a meaningful connection to divine openness or opportunity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Pethahiah was the father of Meshezabel, as stated explicitly in Nehemiah 11:24. Beyond this, no other family relationships are mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Pethahiah's significance lies in his official role as the king's representative, entrusted with authority over the people. This position underscores the administrative and spiritual restoration efforts in Judah following the exile, demonstrating the organized leadership working under God's providence. His inclusion in the genealogical and leadership records affirms the continuity of God's covenant people and their governance.
